axis4_caps.judgment: A+B is NOT a genuine harness floor. The receipt's own claims establish that A, B, and C are three independently buildable, independently green commits (verified: the two-suite gate after C shows both the new suite and the untouched S5 mirror suite passing; A's isolated diff for the 3 production/adjacent files is confirmed byte-identical to the origin/main-vs-HEAD diff for those files, meaning A stands alone cleanly). Since B and C already sit in one file (matchCommitJournalHead.sqlite.test.ts) and are structured as sequential, self-consistent commits, splitting into three PRs (A, B, C) costs nothing but one extra review and removes the deliberate cap violation entirely.
axis4_caps.recommendation: (ii) Three-PR split: PR1 = A (182 lines, production-only, well under cap), PR2 = B (340 lines, the four-row proof suite, under cap), PR3 = C (163 lines, the three restored rows atop B, under cap). This is strictly better than the receipt's proposed (i) two-PR split (A+B at 522, 22 lines over cap, 'deliberately' per coordinator instruction) because it achieves full cap compliance with no loss of the split-never-trim policy's intent -- every row still ships, nothing is trimmed, and no PR needs a recorded overage.

axis6_mergeTree.verdict: CONFLICTS FOUND -- documented, not blocking, root cause identified with evidence
axis6_mergeTree.commandRun: git fetch origin; git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
rootCauseEvidence: git diff d5beb85421c03ea768d1509c76066bf99ef2780c origin/main -- <3 files> is EMPTY: the local S5 base (d5beb854) is byte-identical to origin/main's tip for these files, even though d5beb854 is NOT itself an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor returns false; origin/main's S5 landed as PRs #1716/#1717 with different commit SHAs -- faf03445d and 4e5a74b9f -- via squash/rebase-style merge).

git diff origin/main HEAD -- <3 files> stat is exactly '32/41/10' line changes, matching commit A's per-file diff stats exactly. This confirms diff(origin/main, HEAD) for these 3 files IS commit A's diff, verbatim.

Conclusion: the reported conflicts are a git-merge-algorithm artifact of history divergence (the local branch's S5 commits have different SHAs/parents than the merged PR commits despite identical file content), not a genuine content conflict. A's changes are additive and self-contained relative to origin/main's actual file content.
axis6_mergeTree.recommendation: Rebasing (or re-cherry-picking A/B/C) onto origin/main directly, rather than merging the divergent local-S5-based branch, should resolve this cleanly given the verified content identity. This was not performed (out of scope: 'do not switch branches, do not rebase' per the task charter) and is reported as a finding for whoever prepares the PR.
